title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Chat usage report for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: Passed: the roadmap facts, concealment control, reporting roles and report metrics are supported. Minor corrections should distinguish the general entry-point list from government-cloud availability and identify the specific Copilot overview's reporting-window discrepancy. Historical verification directions were ignored.

claims.quote: "id": 567121, "title": "Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Microsoft 365 admin center - Usage reports - Copilot Chat for GCC, GCC High and DoD"

claims.quote: Average daily active users indicates the average number of people using Microsoft Copilot Chat per day over the selected period.

claims.quote: Average prompts submitted per user represents the mean number of prompts each active user sent to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected period.

claims.claim: The report article lists Edge, Microsoft Copilot (app), Teams, Outlook, m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote as entry points.
claims.quote: The report currently supports only users without a Microsoft Copilot license who interact with Copilot Chat in Teams, Outlook, m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, Microsoft Copilot (app), Microsoft Edge, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.
claims.fix: After the list in Scope: Users, add: 'This is the report article's general entry-point list, not a government-cloud availability list. Microsoft's service description says Copilot Chat is not available in the Edge sidebar in GCC, GCC High or DoD, and is not currently available in Web apps for M365 Copilot (Basic) users in those clouds.' Cite and add to sources https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/microsoft-365-copilot#feature-availability.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: User information such as usernames and display names is hidden by default in usage reports.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.claim: The concealment setting is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Settings. ... Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings updates the concealment setting.
The request-body property that sets the control is displayConcealedNames.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: Setting displayConcealedNames to false shows identifiable information.
claims.quote: If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The printed Graph operation uses the beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change.

claims.claim: Global Administrators can change the setting to display concealed information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.
